claim: Self-repair efficacy is bottlenecked by the model's ability to generate useful feedback on its own code, not by its ability to generate code; using a stronger model to generate feedback significantly improves self-repair's effectiveness for a weaker drafter.
stance_target: adversarial/second-pass review helps when the reviewer is meaningfully stronger than the drafter
scope_conditions: HumanEval and APPS benchmarks, Code Llama, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 as code/feedback models
quoted_support: self-repair is bottlenecked by the model's ability to provide feedback on its own code; using a stronger model [for feedback] ... self-repair still lags far behind what can be achieved with human-level debugging.

claim: When the cost of additional model invocations is accounted for, self-repair is not a silver bullet: several settings show no improvement or only modest improvement over not repairing at all.
stance_target: adding a second model pass to critique/repair code reliably produces net-positive value once cost is considered
quoted_support: Self-repair is not a silver bullet: when the cost of repair is taken into account, we find several settings... modest to no improvements

claim: Self-repair is more likely to be beneficial when more of the sampling budget is spent on generating diverse initial candidates rather than on repair iterations.
stance_target: optimal allocation of compute budget between generation and critique/repair passes
quoted_support: Self-repair is more likely to be beneficial when more of the sampling budget is spent on generating [initial candidates]
